key_insight: HDC-FL uses similarities between client-specific classifier heads to personalize encoder sharing, improving tail-client performance without averaging heads.
engineering_relevance: The method adds personalized encoder mixtures to shared-encoder training without a second optimization trajectory, an extra local objective, or post-training fine-tuning.
method: Periodically project cached classifier heads into normalized, low-rank descriptors and cluster clients.
Build one encoder prototype per cluster from cached client encoders.
Return a soft mixture of encoder prototypes to each client, paired with its own unchanged head.
evidence_signal: Across 11 CIFAR-10/100 configurations with label-subset, Dirichlet, and rotation heterogeneity using ResNet-18 and MobileNetV2, HDC-FL achieves competitive macro-averaged mean accuracy and numerically highest macro-averaged worst-client and bottom-20% accuracy among evaluated methods.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the reported image-classification benchmarks; robustness of head-derived clusters in other tasks and deployment conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: From Classifier Heads to Encoder Prototypes: Personalized Federated Learning with Head-Derived Clustering
